Isolation mengatur apa yang boleh terlih: Isolation controls what may be visible
Isolation level adalah aturan tentang da: An isolation level governs which committed data a statement in one transaction may see while another transaction runs. It is not a switch that automatically makes every business rule correct, a synonym for a row lock, or a promise that two sessions will stop waiting for one another. PostgreSQL uses MVCC: a statement reads row versions that match its snapshot, while an ordinary reader need not wait for a writer merely because the writer is making a new version. The first questions should therefore be specific: when was this snapshot taken, which statement uses it, and does the operation also try to lock or change a row?
Dalam lesson ini, angka saldo dan urutan: In this lesson, balance numbers and event order are an authored trace. The result table shows a visibility prediction for an explicitly written schedule, not the result of two PostgreSQL connections actually running. This boundary matters: learners may build a snapshot mental model, but must not conclude that a lock, commit, or SQLSTATE was observed. In production, an isolation choice still needs to be paired with invariants, writer paths, timeouts, retries, and appropriate operational evidence.
Read Committed mengambil snapshot baru u: Read Committed takes a new snapshot for each statement
Read Committed adalah default PostgreSQL: Read Committed is PostgreSQL's default. A SELECT without a locking clause sees rows committed before that SELECT began. If A performs its first SELECT when the balance is 100000, then B commits a receipt and the balance becomes 125000, A's second SELECT can see 125000 because the second statement takes a new snapshot. A does not see B's still-uncommitted change. Two SELECTs in one transaction can differ; the same transaction boundary does not turn Read Committed into one snapshot.
Untuk command yang mencari lalu mengubah: For a command that finds and then changes rows, Read Committed has an additional detail: the command finds targets from its initial snapshot, may wait for an updater that locked a row first, and then re-evaluates the condition on the updated version. This behavior suits simple operations on predetermined rows, but is not automatically safe for aggregate checks involving many rows. Do not translate “committed” into “every business invariant is protected”; isolation and guard design solve different problems.
Repeatable Read dan Serializable bukan k: Repeatable Read and Serializable are not the same thing
Repeatable Read memakai snapshot sejak s: Repeatable Read uses a snapshot from the first non-control statement in the transaction, and later SELECTs continue to see commits from before that snapshot. Changes made by the transaction itself remain visible to that transaction even before commit. PostgreSQL also prevents phantom reads in Repeatable Read, although the SQL standard requires only a lower minimum of protection. If a Repeatable Read transaction tries to lock or change a row that changed since its snapshot, it may receive a serialization failure and must retry the whole transaction from the beginning.
Serializable memakai visibility snapshot: Serializable uses similar snapshot visibility, then monitors dependencies to reject a commit result that is inconsistent with every possible serial order. PostgreSQL does not promise that every Serializable transaction will succeed or never wait: a conflict can end as a serialization failure, commonly SQLSTATE 40001, and the caller must retry with a new transaction. PostgreSQL memakai multiversion concurre: PostgreSQL uses multiversion concurrency control. Mentally, an UPDATE does not merely replace one number in place; it creates a new version and lets a snapshot choose which version is visible based on transaction status. An ordinary reader can read the appropriate committed version without taking a row lock against the writer. This helps concurrency, but does not mean every old version is available forever, every query sees the same historical state, or vacuum and storage details can be ignored.
Snapshot juga bukan salinan yang boleh d: A snapshot is not a copy that may be edited arbitrarily either. It is a visibility rule for a statement or transaction. Data uncommitted by another session does not become visible merely because it has been written to a buffer. Conversely, a transaction normally sees its own writes because its next decisions must work from changes it made itself. This lesson uses invoice status to make the distinction clear: A can continue seeing open from an old snapshot, but after A writes review, A must be able to read review.
Snapshot Repeatable Read tetap melihat o: A Repeatable Read snapshot still sees own writes
Dalam Repeatable Read, snapshot utama di: In Repeatable Read, the main snapshot is taken at the first non-transaction-control statement and does not move with later concurrent commits. This is not a dirty read; paid is a real committed version in the story, but that commit happened after A's snapshot. RR gives a stable view of concurrent data, not permission to guess facts that did not exist when the snapshot was made.
Ada aturan penting yang sebenarnya bukan: There is an important rule that is not really an exception: A's own changes remain visible to A. Because B did not touch row 502, A can UPDATE row 502 from pending to review, then SELECT row 502 sees review even though A's transaction has not committed. If A instead tries to UPDATE row 501 that B already changed, that is not a successful own-write example; Repeatable Read can abort the transaction with SQLSTATE 40001 and the whole unit must be retried.
Snapshot stabil bukan sertifikat konsist: A stable snapshot is not a business-consistency certificate
Snapshot yang stabil membantu pembacaan: A stable snapshot helps reads that require a consistent answer, but does not automatically guarantee a Payment Ledger invariant. Two transactions can read the same condition and then make different decisions; when each writes a different row, this pattern can become write skew under snapshot isolation. Repeatable Read can still have a serialization anomaly, and a writing transaction can receive a serialization failure when the row it wants to change has changed. Serializable adds dependency monitoring to reject a result without a serial order, so one transaction can receive SQLSTATE 40001, but the caller still must handle retries.

FOR UPDATE menambahkan koordinasi pada p: FOR UPDATE adds coordination to a read
SELECT biasa memakai MVCC snapshot dan u: An ordinary SELECT uses an MVCC snapshot and generally does not wait for a row writer. SELECT FOR UPDATE adds intent: a found row is treated as though it will be updated, so the transaction takes a row-level lock. This lock prevents another transaction from running a conflicting UPDATE, DELETE, or locking clause on that row until the lock-holding transaction ends. A lock is not merely a label in a SELECT result; it is coordination that affects other writers and lockers.
Row lock juga tidak berarti seluruh tabe: A row lock also does not mean the whole table or every reader stops. PostgreSQL documentation says a row-level lock does not affect ordinary data querying; it blocks writers and lockers on the same row. The lock normally lasts until the end of the transaction and can be released when a savepoint is rolled back. Therefore a transaction holding a lock should be short and should not wait for human input or a network provider.
NOWAIT dan SKIP LOCKED memilih trade-off: NOWAIT and SKIP LOCKED choose different trade-offs
Dengan NOWAIT, SELECT FOR UPDATE tidak m: With NOWAIT, SELECT FOR UPDATE does not wait for a conflicting row; the statement reports an error immediately. In PostgreSQL, this row-lock conflict uses SQLSTATE 55P03 with condition name `lock_not_available`. This fits when the caller should return “try again” or choose another path rather than hold the request. The error is not proof that a payment failed, not a reason to swallow the exception, and not a result that can be turned into success without deciding the transaction state. The application needs to understand the SQLSTATE or error contract from its driver and choose retry/backoff separately.
Dengan SKIP LOCKED, row yang belum bisa: With SKIP LOCKED, a row that cannot yet be locked is skipped. This is useful for multiple queue consumers that want other work, but the result is deliberately inconsistent as a general view: returned rows are not a complete list of matching rows at that time. An empty result set also does not prove the queue is empty; every matching row may be temporarily locked. SKIP LOCKED is not appropriate for a complete balance report and does not prove a skipped row has finished processing. A queue still needs business status, a lease or timeout, retries, and idempotency.
Lock tidak menghapus semua risiko concur: A lock does not remove every concurrency risk
FOR UPDATE mengunci row yang dipilih, bu: FOR UPDATE locks selected rows, not an abstract predicate for every row that might appear later. Two transactions locking several rows in different orders can still deadlock; PostgreSQL detects the deadlock and aborts one of them. A consistent lock order reduces the risk, but the caller still needs retries for deadlocks and serialization failures. NOWAIT turns waiting into an error, while SKIP LOCKED turns the result into a subset; neither replaces an invariant or business key.
